target.name: NetworkOcean
target.founder: Sam Mendel (CEO; serial founder, prior exit of a creator-hiring marketplace), Eric Kim (CTO; ex-Palantir, Merge; Cornell)

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $1M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
NetworkOcean is a Seed-stage ocean and maritime technology company founded by Sam Mendel (serial founder with prior marketplace exit) and Eric Kim (ex-Palantir, Merge engineering lead). The company has raised $1M to date. The comparable universe consists of three private peers in the ocean tech space—Standard Subsea, Clippership, and Albacore—with no direct public market comps available for this frontier subsector.

The analysis applies a stage-progression methodology, which is the applicable triangulation approach given data availability. Using the $1M in total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $2M. This single-method result anchors the quantitative assessment.

The triangulated valuation range is $2.1M (low) to $2.9M (high), with a median of $2M. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single methodology; the range widens only modestly to account for typical variance in stage-progression assumptions. Key uncertainties include the absence of public comparables and limited private comp depth, which constrains calibration of the step-up multiple. Additionally, the frontier nature of ocean tech limits historical precedent for value creation at this stage. Material upside or downside would depend on product-market validation, unit economics, and capital efficiency relative to the stated peer set.
